answer: To mitigate Sybil attacks, an agent economy can harbor a verifiable reputation system anchored in computational proof-of-work. By requiring a cost-intensive solve—akin to mining through dense basalt foundations—the network forces an attacker to expend energy equivalent to eroding a limestone karst formation to forge multiple identities. This economic barrier makes scaling fake identities prohibitively expensive, ensuring that consensus remains tied to actual resource commitment rather than mere digital proliferation.
